title: Sample-Specific Output Constraints for Neural Networks
authors: Mathis Brosowsky, Florian Keck, Olaf Dünkel, Marius Zöllner
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI-21), vol. 35, no. 8
conclusions: Introduces ConstraintNet, which applies an input-dependent parametrization of the network's output space so that every prediction is guaranteed, by construction, to lie inside a per-sample convex-polytope constraint region (no post-hoc projection or clipping needed).
Uses a vertex representation of the convex polytope so an auxiliary tensor input can specify a different constraint per sample, supporting multiple/varying constraints across the dataset.
The layer is end-to-end trainable with negligible extra forward/backward compute, and fully covers the interior of the constrained region (unlike projection-based approaches).
Demonstrated on facial landmark detection (CNN with a ConstraintNet output layer) and on a safe-RL vehicle controller task, showing constraint satisfaction with competitive/improved performance.
Positions the method for safety-critical deployment where hard per-sample output guarantees are required, in contrast to soft-penalty training.
